title: Buddha
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Osamu Tezuka's retelling of the life of Siddhartha, from sickly prince to wandering ascetic to enlightened teacher, set in a turbulent ancient India of wars, bandits and caste oppression. Invented characters such as the animal-possessing bandit Tatta, the slave-caste woman Migaila and the wolf-raised Devadatta surround the historical story. Tezuka, described by his publisher as a humanist rather than a Buddhist, mixes philosophy with action, slapstick and anachronistic jokes. Eisner Award winner; eight volumes in English.
life_message: Enlightenment comes from seeing that all life is connected and answering suffering with compassion rather than revenge.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Religious quest, yet Tezuka's humanist questioning of ritual.

folkways.japan: Reflects Japan's Mahayana Buddhist heritage and Tezuka's postwar humanism and anti-war anxieties, including nuclear imagery.

delivery.evidence: ANN: philosophy made believable through dialogue and action, not preachy; the Buddha states his teachings outright as a preacher.
delivery.note: Revenge-seekers get full arcs, while Hindu ritual and caste are mainly shown through their harms, per the publisher and ANN.

winners_losers: Siddhartha's way of compassion prevails; caste oppressors and the violent are shown as causing suffering; sympathy goes to the outcast and the converted.
